title: Find the Words That Prove It
observable_outcome: Answer a specific-information question and copy the exact notice words that support the answer.
learning_objective: Use question keywords to scan a short notice, select relevant evidence, and give an evidence-based answer.

scenario.prompt: AIRPORT SHUTTLE CHANGE. Friday only. The airport shuttle leaves from Gate B, not Gate A. Last departure: 18:40. Hotel guests need a blue ticket.
scenario.model: Where should you wait? Gate B. Evidence: The airport shuttle leaves from Gate B, not Gate A.

language.grammar: Short notices often omit full sentences: Last departure: 18:40 means The last departure is at 18:40. Your answer may be short if the evidence is copied clearly.
language.meaning: Evidence is the exact part of the notice that makes an answer reasonable. The answer Gate B is supported by the line naming Gate B as the departure point.
language.appropriateness: For practical notices, scan for the detail asked about rather than reading every word at the same speed. Copy only enough text to prove the answer without changing its meaning.
language.time_phrase: 18:50 is after 18:40, so a traveller arriving at 18:50 cannot take the last shuttle described by this notice.

activities.prompt: Where should you wait for the shuttle?

options.feedback: Yes. The notice says the shuttle leaves from Gate B, not Gate A.
No. Gate A appears only as the old or rejected location. The words not Gate A rule it out.
No. The notice mentions hotel guests but gives no lobby departure point.

activities.prompt: Which words prove the last shuttle leaves before 19:00?

options.feedback: Correct. This line gives the last time, and 18:40 is twenty minutes before 19:00.
This gives the day, not the departure time. It cannot prove the before-19:00 answer.

options.text: Hotel guests need a blue ticket.
options.feedback: This gives a ticket rule. It does not contain time evidence.

activities.prompt: You arrive at 18:50. Can you take this shuttle?

options.feedback: Yes. The answer and copied time agree: 18:50 is after the last departure.
No. The relevant boundary is 18:40, not 19:00. Use the notice's exact cutoff.
Friday is required, but the arrival is still ten minutes after the last departure.

transfer.situation: LIBRARY - SATURDAY. Open: 09:00-13:00. Help desk closes at 12:30. Returns box stays open all day.
transfer.task: At 12:45, can you ask the help desk for assistance? Answer yes or no. Then copy the words that prove your answer.
acceptable_responses: No. Evidence: Help desk closes at 12:30.
No - the notice says, 'Help desk closes at 12:30.'
You cannot ask the help desk at 12:45 because it closes at 12:30.
rubric: The evidence names the help desk.
The answer connects 12:45 with the earlier closing time.

review_prompt: Tomorrow, explain the five-step reading path: question, key word, scan, evidence, answer.

visual.alt_text: A four-stage evidence path: ask where to wait, scan the shuttle notice, highlight Gate B not Gate A, then answer Gate B with the supporting line.
visual.text_equivalent: QUESTION: Where should you wait? -> SCAN: look for gate -> EVIDENCE: leaves from Gate B, not Gate A -> ANSWER: Gate B.

scenes.title: Notice
scenes.caption: AIRPORT SHUTTLE CHANGE
scenes.explanation: First identify the type of text and the practical situation.

scenes.title: Question
scenes.caption: Where should you wait?
scenes.explanation: The question tells you to look for a place, especially a gate.

scenes.title: Scan
scenes.caption: Gate B ... not Gate A
scenes.explanation: Move your eyes to the gate words instead of rereading every line equally.

scenes.title: Evidence
scenes.caption: The shuttle leaves from Gate B, not Gate A.
scenes.explanation: Copy the smallest complete line that proves the location.

scenes.title: Answer
scenes.caption: Gate B.
scenes.explanation: Give the answer, then connect it to the evidence when explanation is required.

scenes.title: Transfer
scenes.caption: Help desk closes at 12:30.
scenes.explanation: Use the same evidence path with a new notice and a new time.
